clue.text: May racing driver set record here? That's a bit of a coincidence

definitions.text: May racing driver set record here?
definitions.meaning: a record-setting driver does so over one circuit of the track, read as two words

definitions.text: That's a bit of a coincidence
definitions.meaning: a partial coinciding or shared stretch between two things

explanation.surface: A remark that a racing driver's record on a particular track is something of a fluke.
explanation.walkthrough: The first half is cryptic: split the answer into OVER LAP, where a driver might set a lap record. 'May' is just 'might', not the month.
explanation.definitionFit: Where two ranges partly share ground, they coincide over a portion, which is exactly a partial match.

clue.text: Royal building too large to be tolerated?

parts.note: OS is the abbreviation for outsize, a clothing size that is too large for most
borne means put up with or tolerated

explanation.surface: A question whether a palace is too big to put up with.
explanation.walkthrough: OSBORNE House on the Isle of Wight was Queen Victoria's country residence.
explanation.definitionFit: Osborne House is a former royal residence, so it is a palace or royal building.

clue.text: Learning from a number of papers about game

indicators.note: the word for papers goes around the game, so it is placed about it

parts.note: an edition is a batch of newspapers printed at one time
RU is rugby union, a football game

explanation.surface: Someone gains knowledge by reading several newspapers about a sport.
explanation.definitionFit: Erudition is deep scholarship, the knowledge acquired through study.

clue.text: This castle's a long way south of the city

definitions.text: This castle's a long way south of the city

parts.words: This castle's a long way south of the city
parts.note: a famous castle in Kent shares its name with a large Yorkshire city far to the north

explanation.surface: A tourist remarks that a castle is nowhere near the city it is named after.
explanation.walkthrough: LEEDS Castle stands in Kent in south-east England, some two hundred miles from the northern city of the same name.
explanation.definitionFit: The castle bears the same name as the city but lies far to the south, in Kent.

clue.text: Soldier extremely eager to join warship

parts.note: a private is the lowest-ranking soldier

indicators.note: extremely means taking only the extreme letters, the first and last, of eager

explanation.surface: A keen soldier wants to sign up for service on a fighting ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely' gives ER, the first and last letters of 'eager'.
explanation.definitionFit: A privateer was an armed privately owned vessel licensed to attack enemy shipping, a type of warship.

clue.text: As a journalist's job usually is, in theory

definitions.text: As a journalist's job usually is
definitions.meaning: a journalist's work normally appears printed in a newspaper
theoretically, as opposed to in practice

explanation.surface: A comment that a reporter's work is, theoretically, what it seems.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that works only in principle looks fine when written down but may fail in practice.

clue.text: Mineral core, unusually hard inside

indicators.note: inside means the hard letter goes within the rearranged word
unusually suggests the letters of core are arranged in an unusual way

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A geologist notes a mineral whose centre is unexpectedly tough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusually' rearranges CORE to OCRE, and 'inside' puts H within it.
explanation.definitionFit: Ochre is an earthy iron-oxide pigment mined from the ground, so it counts as a mineral.

clue.text: Recommendation to run through capital is not disinterested

indicators.note: through means the pieces pass into the middle of the city name

parts.note: Paris is the capital of France
a tip is a piece of advice or recommendation
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A suggested route across a capital city is said to be biased.
explanation.walkthrough: PARTI PRIS is French for a preconceived view; used as an adjective it means prejudiced. 'to' and 'is' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: A parti pris position is a biased, prejudiced one, the opposite of impartial.

clue.text: Not flush? May look flushed, so

definitions.meaning: sticking out from a surface rather than level with it
someone pleased with an achievement may go red with self-satisfaction

explanation.surface: A remark about a person who is short of money yet looks red in the face.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flush' tempts as 'rich', but here it is the carpenter's sense of level with a surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Projecting beyond a surface is called standing out; a self-satisfied person may glow with pleasure.

clue.text: Official procedure that's legally binding

parts.note: bureaucratic formality, read literally as the coloured ribbon once used to tie up legal documents

explanation.surface: A description of a formal process that has the force of law.
explanation.definitionFit: Bureaucratic rules are named after the coloured ribbon lawyers literally bound their papers with.

clue.text: Beast runs in interior of Scottish island

indicators.note: in interior of means placed inside the island's name

parts.note: Bute is an island in the Firth of Clyde
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: An animal charges about the inland parts of an island off Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: A brute is a wild animal, as opposed to a human being.

clue.text: Writer takes one to the forest

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
Sherwood is the famous forest of Robin Hood in Nottinghamshire

explanation.surface: An author brings someone along to the woods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'takes' and 'to' simply join the pieces. Christopher ISHERWOOD wrote the Berlin stories behind Cabaret.
explanation.definitionFit: Christopher Isherwood was an Anglo-American novelist, so he is a writer.

clue.text: Restore returning monarch with all due ceremony

indicators.note: returning means the abbreviation for the monarch is read backwards

parts.note: ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen
in state means with full formal pomp

explanation.surface: A king coming home is put back on the throne with full pageantry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' turns ER round to RE.
explanation.definitionFit: To reinstate is to put someone back in a former position, to restore them.

clue.text: In centres of Hindu art can see this deity?

indicators.note: centres of means taking the central letters of each of the following words

explanation.surface: A question whether a Hindu god can be seen at the heart of Hindu art.
explanation.walkthrough: The centres are IND from Hindu, R from art and A from can. 'In' and 'see this' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: Indra is the Vedic king of the gods, lord of thunder and rain.

clue.text: Order return of fish caught

indicators.note: return of means the fish's name is read backwards

parts.note: the ide is a freshwater fish
CT is a scorecard abbreviation for caught in cricket

explanation.surface: An instruction to send back a fish that has been landed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return of' turns IDE into EDI.
explanation.definitionFit: An edict is an official decree or command.

clue.text: Tense supporter of highly dangerous performance

definitions.text: Tense supporter of highly dangerous performance

parts.words: Tense supporter of highly dangerous performance
parts.note: a taut line holding up a performer who walks high above the circus ring

explanation.surface: A nervous fan watching a risky show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tense' reads as anxious, but it describes the stretched line itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A high-wire act is performed on a taut cable that bears the walker's weight.

clue.text: Skill shown by priest swimming in river

indicators.note: in means the rearranged letters go inside the river's name

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon

indicators.note: swimming suggests the letters of priest moving about

explanation.surface: A clergyman shows prowess by bathing in a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swimming' rearranges PRIEST to PERTIS, which goes inside EXE.
explanation.definitionFit: Expertise is specialist know-how, a high level of ability.

clue.text: Quietly pointed to favourite

parts.note: P is piano, the musical direction for quietly
referred to means indicated or mentioned

explanation.surface: Someone discreetly indicates the one they like best.
explanation.definitionFit: A preferred option is the one favoured above others.

clue.text: Fancy one girl that's averse to being embraced

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: being embraced means held within the girl's name

parts.note: Mary is a girl's name
agin is dialect for against, opposed to

explanation.surface: Imagine a girl who does not like being hugged.
explanation.walkthrough: AGIN is an informal word for 'against'. 'that's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Something imaginary exists only in fancy, the imagination, as in a fanciful notion.

clue.text: Contents of Ark emerge in a muddle

indicators.note: a muddle is a confused jumble, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: Noah's animals come out in a disorderly crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'muddle' rearranges EMERGE IN A.
explanation.definitionFit: Noah's Ark held a collection of animals, which is what a menagerie is.

clue.text: Turned up information in memory identifying Spanish killer

indicators.note: turned up in a down clue means the whole assembled piece is read from bottom to top
in means the information goes inside the memory abbreviation

parts.note: ROM is read-only memory in computing
data means information

explanation.surface: Someone recalls information that names a Spanish murderer.
explanation.walkthrough: DATA inside ROM gives RODATAM, which 'Turned up' reverses.
explanation.definitionFit: A matador is the bullfighter who kills the bull in a Spanish bullfight.

clue.text: Brave decision to take off the top of one's head like this?

definitions.text: Brave decision to take off the top of one's head like this?

parts.words: Brave decision to take off the top of one's head like this?
parts.note: a warrior's choice to remove the hair and skin from the crown of a foe's head

explanation.surface: A courageous choice made on the spur of the moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brave' looks like courageous, but it is an old word for a Native American warrior; 'off the top of one's head' suggests improvisation.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking a trophy of skin and hair from an enemy's head was a warrior's practice, as described.

clue.text: Breathe hard, about to ligature one in surgery, perhaps

indicators.note: about means the panting word goes around the ligature word

parts.note: pant means breathe hard and fast
a tie is a binding or ligature

explanation.surface: A surgeon breathes heavily before tying off a vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link. 'perhaps' marks a doctor's surgery as one example of where a sick person is found.
explanation.definitionFit: A sick person in a doctor's surgery or on the operating table is under treatment.

clue.text: Apocryphal story of American's worthless wife rejected

indicators.note: rejected means the wife is thrown out of the word

parts.note: two-bit is American slang for cheap or worthless

explanation.surface: A tale told about an American's no-good spouse being cast aside.
explanation.walkthrough: The Book of TOBIT is in the Apocrypha. 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Tobit is a book of the Apocrypha telling the tale of a devout Israelite.

clue.text: Attack and defeat, capturing enemy leader

indicators.note: capturing means the word for defeat holds the letter inside it

parts.note: to best someone is to beat them

indicators.note: leader means the first letter of enemy

explanation.surface: An army assaults and beats its foes, taking their commander prisoner.
explanation.definitionFit: To beset is to assail or harass from all sides.

clue.text: Branch I grafted into exhausted garden plant

indicators.note: grafted into means the pieces are set inside, as a cutting is inserted into stock

parts.note: spent means used up or exhausted
an arm is a branch, as of a river or organisation

explanation.surface: A gardener grafts a cutting into a worn-out plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Spearmint is a common herb grown in gardens.

clue.text: Call in turn to get round

definitions.meaning: a person's turn to buy the drinks for a group

explanation.surface: A person is told it is their go to buy the drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link. 'My shout' is everyday British for 'my turn to pay'.
explanation.definitionFit: A loud cry is a yell; in pub slang it is one's turn to stand a round of drinks.

clue.text: Catholic priest concealing sacred object

indicators.note: concealing means the Catholic abbreviation hides the priest inside it

parts.note: RC stands for Roman Catholic
Eli was the priest who raised Samuel in the Bible

explanation.surface: A Catholic cleric hides a holy item.
explanation.definitionFit: A relic is a venerated object, such as a saint's remains or belongings.

clue.text: I almost achieved distinction in grim, shameful state

indicators.note: in means the pieces go inside the word for grim

parts.note: dour means stern and grim

indicators.note: almost means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: shone means excelled or stood out

explanation.surface: Someone nearly gained honours but ended up in disgrace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims SHONE to SHON; I plus SHON goes inside DOUR.
explanation.definitionFit: Dishonour is disgrace, a condition of shame.

clue.text: Without money up front, satisfy legal agreement

indicators.note: without means the money letter is taken away
up front means the letter removed is the one at the start

parts.note: to please is to satisfy
P is penny or pence, money

explanation.surface: A tenant without cash in advance must meet the terms of a contract.
explanation.definitionFit: A lease is a contract granting use of property for a time.

clue.text: Go back to buy another round?

definitions.meaning: treat someone again, read as a word with a 're-' prefix

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether to return to the bar for more drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link. The second sense splits the answer as RE-TREAT, to treat again.
explanation.definitionFit: To withdraw is to pull back; to stand drinks again is to treat once more.

clue.text: Unscramble call received in small branch

indicators.note: received in means the call is taken inside the branch abbreviation

parts.note: dept is the short form of department, a branch of an organisation
cry means call out

explanation.surface: A phone call comes in to a small office of a company.
explanation.definitionFit: To decrypt a coded message is to decode it.
